mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a negative predictor of S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, meaning that the market always reacts negatively to the current level of the federal funds rate, regardless of its absolute value.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of cases where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in the last month, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized CPI growth rate above 2% in the last month signals inflationary pressure that forces central banks to tighten, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL annualized growth rate > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized growth rate exceeds 2% in the last month, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market tightening, which, when combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100), signals rising inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises, and INDPRO < 100
regime_hint: labor market tightening with weak supply
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where UNRATE falls, PAYEMS rises, and INDPRO < 100, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Weak consumer demand (RSAFS < 500000) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates a broad economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where RSAFS < 500000 and INDPRO < 100, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), a rise in annualized CPI growth above 2% signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL annualized growth rate > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL annualized growth rate exceeds 2% in the last month, the 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 100, the 5-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a weak supply regime (INDPRO < 100), a strong consumer demand (RSAFS > 500000) indicates a rebound in economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 100 and RSAFS > 500000, the 60-day forward returns are positive.
